question.question: After application completion attempts an automatic joint-exit proposal while leadership transfer is pending, does transfer timeout restore a path to automatic exit without an unrelated client proposal or new election?
question.importance: A quiescent cluster could remain in the joint voter configuration, retaining outgoing quorum requirements and delaying completion of a requested membership transition. This is a bounded liveness and configuration-completion question, not an asserted safety failure.
contexts: A stable leader with a failed bounded transfer
No unrelated client proposals after joint configuration application
event_paths: Committed implicit-joint entry -> ApplyConfChange -> begin transfer before completion acknowledgment -> appliedTo -> rejected internal exit proposal -> transfer timeout -> healthy quorum processing

supporting_behavior_ids.b_config: Installs applied joint configuration and AutoLeave policy.

counterevidence: Transfer timeout clears the admission block; later application completion retries automatic exit.
Successful transfer gives a new leader an empty log entry whose completion can retrigger exit.
No obligation requires arbitrary client proposals to commit, and generic ReadIndex loss permission is unrelated to automatic exit.
unknowns: A fresh fixed check must correlate the installed joint change, application acknowledgment, expired transfer and bounded final observation.
No API deadline is specified; distinguish a finite non-completion measurement from the source-supported absence of an autonomous retry trigger.
question.trigger_rationale: Exploration 1514d7be2baa4094be4f4a559ea73ade reached the legal overlap, timed out the transfer and remained joint after serviced ticks; control and rescue both exited. Source locates automatic exit only in application completion, so a fixed check can observe the stall while preserving the lack of an API deadline.

obligation.description: For an applied implicit joint configuration, Raft owns the automatic proposal of the exit transition when safe. If an internal exit proposal is temporarily rejected during leadership transfer and that transfer fails, a stable leader with both quorums available must retain an autonomous path to retry and finish the exit; it must not require an unrelated client proposal or another leadership change merely to recover that internal work.

scope.description: Implicit automatic joint transitions, with legal serialized RawNode application, failed transient leadership transfer, continuing ticks, prompt persistence/application and reliable quorum communication after the dropped transfer request.
assumptions: No crashes or storage failures; caller completes Ready persistence and application before Advance.
Both joint majorities remain responsive and same leader remains authoritative.
No further configuration requests or ordinary client proposals are supplied during the observation interval.
excluded: Explicit joint transitions whose exit belongs to the caller.
Permanent quorum loss, successful leadership transfer, or caller failure to process Ready.
A universal numeric completion deadline or proof of all-history liveness.
Consensus safety, client data loss and availability consequences beyond joint-state retention.

grounding.derivation: raft.proto assigns implicit joint exit to Raft, contrasting explicit mode where the application must propose exit, and promises automatic transition when safe. appliedTo identifies transfer rejection as temporary and explicitly expects automatic retry after transfer failure or completion under a new leader. Hence an unrelated external proposal is not an assigned prerequisite. The implementation calls appliedTo only on nonempty application responses or snapshot completion; transfer abort clears the field without rescheduling the internal attempt. This establishes a responsibility to retain autonomous retry, not an API-specified number of ticks. A bounded checker can measure non-completion under serviced work; source review is necessary to interpret the missing trigger.
grounding.applicability: The joint entry is genuinely replicated, committed and applied. The same leader survives a transfer whose TimeoutNow is dropped; quorum responses continue. No early Advance or fabricated acknowledgments are used.
unresolved: The API gives no numeric deadline; any finite final-state comparison has that limitation and must not be reported as an unconditional eventual-liveness proof.
alternatives: A subsequent application completion retries successfully, as the exploration rescue demonstrates, but requires additional work not guaranteed in a quiescent cluster.
A successful transfer elects a new leader and can supply a new application event; the selected history instead lets the transfer timeout.

rationale: Exploration resolves the main construction uncertainty; fix the automatic-retry responsibility independently of its observed failure and retain the numeric-deadline limitation.

feedback.answered: Exploration observed control final state outgoing=0 and AutoLeave=false at index 4. Failed-transfer case dropped one actual TimeoutNow, remained leader in term 2, cleared transferee by tick 10, and retained joint state with applied=commit=last=3 through tick 40. A later ordinary proposal caused automatic exit at index 5. This excludes the explanation that ordinary serviced ticks/heartbeats in this schedule provide the missing application trigger. It is construction knowledge, not formal property Evidence.
